title: The Armenian Genocide
subject: histoire
description: Between **1915** and **1916**, the Ottoman government organized the deportation and systematic extermination of a large part of the Armenian population of the Empire.

hero.hook: The first genocide of the 20th century, long unnamed, still at the heart of a battle for the truth.

blocks.text: Between **1915** and **1916**, in the midst of World War I, the government of the Ottoman Empire orchestrated the extermination of a large part of its Armenian population. About **two thirds** of the Armenians of the empire perished.

This crime, estimated at between **600,000** and **1.5 million** deaths, would later push jurists to coin a new word: . This is how an ancestral minority was designated as the enemy from within, then destroyed. [[genocide]]

Armenians are one of the oldest Christian populations in Anatolia, the heart of present-day Turkey. In the Ottoman Empire, the  system gave them religious autonomy, but an inferior status. In the 19th century, the empire declined. Nationalism is on the rise. The Armenians are gradually seen as an internal threat, close to Russia. [[millet]]

The  (**1894-1896**), under Sultan Abdülhamid II, are already **100,000** to **300,000** dead. They remain unpunished. In **1908**, the , a nationalist movement, initially aroused hope. Then three men, **Send**, **Talaat** and **Cemal**, imposed radical nationalism: an ethnically homogeneous Türkiye, with no place for non-Muslim minorities. [[The Hamidian massacres (1894-1896)]] [[Young Turks]]

The world war accelerates everything. After the Ottoman defeat at Sarikamis (January 1915), Enver Pasha accused the Armenian soldiers of treason. On **April 24, 1915**, in Constantinople, the capital, more than **200** intellectuals and notables were arrested, then executed. This date has become that of global commemoration.
The Polish jurist **Raphael Lemkin**, when later coining the word “genocide”, was thinking explicitly of the Armenians. The UN  (1948) follows from this. [[The legal definition of genocide]]

In May, a deportation law provided a legal framework for expulsions to the deserts of Mesopotamia. Men are often massacred as soon as they leave the villages. Women, children and old people are pushed into forced marches, without food or protection.

sections.title: Deir ez-Zor and the end of a world

blocks.text: Survivors end up in rudimentary camps in the Syrian desert, notably at **Deir ez-Zor**. In 1916, the last survivors were still eliminated there, or died of exhaustion and epidemics. Neutral diplomats, such as the American **Henry Morgenthau**, describe “race murder”.

In Anatolia, churches and property are destroyed or confiscated. Three millennia of continuous Armenian presence on these lands are coming to an end. After the war, the main leaders fled. The emerging Republic of Türkiye practices a policy of official oblivion. The survivors form a huge , a community scattered across the world. [[diaspora]]

Even today, Turkey recognizes suffering and massacres in the chaos of war, but rejects the term genocide. Faced with this denial of the State, the diaspora is campaigning for recognition. France (2001) and the United States (2021), among others, have officially recognized the genocidal nature of the facts.

blocks.text: Between **1915** and **1916**, the Ottoman Empire organized the methodical extermination of hundreds of thousands of Armenians. This crime forces the world to invent the word , the recognition of which remains a political issue. [[genocide]]
